# SECURITY: This lock file pins all direct and transitive Python dependencies to exact
# versions with SHA256 hashes. It mitigates supply-chain attacks where a compromised
# package could execute code during installation or import and exfiltrate credentials
# (GITHUB_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, NVD_API_KEY, LACUNA_TOKEN) that are present in
# later workflow steps.
#
# DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE MANUALLY.
#
# To regenerate after changing requirements.txt:
#   1. Create a clean virtual environment: python3 -m venv /tmp/fissure-lock
#   2. Activate it: source /tmp/fissure-lock/bin/activate
#   3. Install pip-tools: pip install pip-tools
#   4. Generate the lock file: pip-compile --generate-hashes --allow-unsafe \
#        --output-file requirements-lock.txt requirements.txt
#   5. Audit the diff for unexpected new packages or major version jumps
#   6. Commit both requirements.txt and requirements-lock.txt together
#
# The --require-hashes flag in workflows enforces that every package (including
# transitive dependencies) must have a hash, preventing pip from silently fetching
# unhashed packages from the index.

# Direct dependencies from requirements.txt:
# httpx>=0.27
# pydantic>=2.12,<3
# PyYAML>=6.0
# pytest>=9.0.3
# google-adk==2.10.0
# litellm==1.102.2
# tokenizers>=0.23.1,<1.0

# BOOTSTRAP INSTRUCTIONS:
# This is a template lock file. Before the workflows can run with --require-hashes,
# you must generate real hashes. Two options:
#
# Option A (recommended): Use pip-compile locally
#   pip install pip-tools
#   pip-compile --generate-hashes --allow-unsafe --output-file requirements-lock.txt requirements.txt
#
# Option B (if pip-compile fails): Bootstrap from a workflow run
#   1. Temporarily change one workflow to use: pip install -r requirements.txt && pip freeze > /tmp/freeze.txt
#   2. Download the freeze.txt artifact
#   3. Run: pip-compile --generate-hashes --allow-unsafe --output-file requirements-lock.txt /tmp/freeze.txt
#   4. Restore the workflow to use requirements-lock.txt with --require-hashes
#
# Until real hashes are present, the workflows will fail with:
# "Hashes are required in --require-hashes mode"
#
# This is intentional: it prevents the workflows from running with unpinned dependencies
# and exposing secrets to potentially compromised packages.

# Placeholder entries (will cause pip to fail until replaced with real hashes):
google-adk==2.10.0
httpx>=0.27
litellm==1.102.2
pydantic>=2.12,<3
pytest>=9.0.3
pyyaml>=6.0
tokenizers>=0.23.1,<1.0
